items.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an image problem - so why is Meta's business booming?
items.summary: A new film paints the Meta founder as a villain. But the tech firm seems immune to bad publicity, writes our North America tech correspondent.
items.content:
Mark Zuckerberg was just three minutes into his keynote speech at the company's annual Meta Connect product event last month when his tone turned almost wistful.

"Building is an act of love," he said, glancing down at the ground with his hands in his pockets. "It's how we impart what we believe, and we pour our hearts and our souls into what we make."

Speaking to hundreds of analysts and developers, Zuckerberg proceeded to share news about Meta's latest AI products: its new agentic chatbot Muse, a slew of smart glasses, as well as a Tamagotchi-like AI gadget users can attach to their wrists.

It was a conference focused on new technologies - but still, it's perhaps notable that during a presentation lasting nearly an hour, Zuckerberg did not mention two of his most popular products, Instagram and Facebook, the social media platforms that have helped Meta become a $2tn company.

For much of the past year, Meta has been embroiled in a series of legal actions, accused of deliberately designing products that are addictive to young users.

That has led to the release of internal emails, corporate documents and whistleblower testimony that personal injury lawyers and prosecutors across the country have wielded to make their case.

And Zuckerberg is unpopular: last year, a Pew Research Center poll found that two-thirds of Americans had an unfavourable opinion of him.

His reputation is unlikely to be helped by The Social Reckoning, a film by Aaron Sorkin released this week. It's about whistleblower claims that Meta executives were aware of their products harming young people. Succession actor Jeremy Strong plays Zuckerberg as a "full-on villain", according to a review in the Hollywood Reporter, "stoically arguing that even the slightest gesture of responsibility is anathema where money is concerned".

Some speculate that this is Meta's "Big Tobacco" moment, with a consensus forming against the company, and the social media industry as a whole.

But the truth seems to be more complicated. Despite months of bad press, in the real world Meta's products are doing better than ever. Use of its apps continues to rise, and users are already flocking to its new AI assistant.

It raises the question: can anything really clip Meta's wings? Or is it now something of a 'Teflon' company, with scandals simply bouncing off it?

Last summer, Reuters revealed that Meta allowed its chatbots to "engage a child in conversations that are romantic or sensual", and provide false medical information to users.

Meta has revised those policies and said that such responses should never have been allowed.

And this year, bills have been mounting. In March, a jury gave $6m (£4.5m) to a 20-year-old California woman who claimed she suffered mental health harms related to her use of Meta's Instagram and Google's YouTube.

Around the same time, New Mexico became the first state to succeed in a lawsuit against Meta over child safety issues. A jury found the company had failed to warn the public about the dangers its platforms posed to kids. Meta was fined a total of $942m. The judge called Meta a "public nuisance" akin to air pollution.

Meta says it disagrees with the verdicts and is appealing both cases.

In May, Meta was among the social companies that avoided a trial by settling a case brought by a Kentucky school district that claimed their product design had led to a youth mental health crisis. Meta reportedly agreed to pay $9m, the most of any defendant.

And this summer, Meta struck a high-profile $18bn settlement with 48 US states, plus the District of Columbia and three US territories. Meta denied wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and during the five-day trial it maintained that it had worked extensively over the years to make its platforms safer for young users, pouring resources into testing and research. As part of the deal, the firm promised to enact two-hour daily time limits for young users, along with night-time blocks on use, muted notifications during school hours, and other changes.

The company faces other lawsuits too, including one starting later this month in Los Angeles, also related to alleged social media addiction among young users.

Meanwhile, several countries have moved to ban social media for children entirely, starting with Australia last December. Social media companies are broadly disliked, even while their products remain wildly popular. A Reuters/Ipsos survey suggests that 85% of Americans think social media can be addictive for children, and 61% support greater government oversight.

"Once the public has stopped trusting you, it's kind of a downward spiral," says associate professor Alison Taylor of New York University's Stern School of Business.

"It feels like… the trust deficit is so big, I just don't know that they're going to be able to recover."

But despite those high-profile cases, the company reported that the number of people using some of its apps (like Instagram and WhatsApp) has risen 3% year on year and this year's second quarter revenue was up 28% compared with the same period in 2025.

While it has agreed to temper its pursuit of the teen market (which many brands eagerly cultivate to build their future user base), the company has said that teens accounted for less than 1% of its revenue anyway. Competitors TikTok and Google's YouTube are more popular with young users.

And the company's settlement with the 48 states was widely considered a massive win for Meta, because it prevented some Meta bosses (including Zuckerberg) from having to give testimony, and stopped the release of further internal documents, while allowing the company to avoid admitting wrongdoing. The company's stock price surged 4% immediately following the announcement, and is up more than 25% over the last month.

One view popular among critics is that the company has tested consumer tolerance for bad behaviour and until now, its business has mostly managed to withstand the blowback. In other words, people will continue to use the products even if they don't like the company.

"I think they're in a remarkably good position that I didn't expect them to be in," says Patrick Moorhead, founder and CEO of Moor Insights & Strategy.

However, Meta's move into AI depends partly on rebuilding public trust.

Last month, the company launched its new AI personal assistant app, Muse. Crucially, Muse is an AI agent, meaning it can carry out tasks in multiple stages and work on something over several hours (in contrast to chatbots like ChatGPT, which tend to do one task at a time).

It's the first AI agent from a major tech firm to become publicly available. A New York Times tech reporter who used the app for two weeks says he was "blown away"; the app called his dental insurer on his behalf, ordered him groceries and tracked his credit card spending in a spreadsheet.

But Muse works best when users hand over some of their most personal information to the company, including credit card information, purchase histories and access to email inboxes.

It's a big ask for a company whose reputation on privacy has been sullied, starting a decade ago with the Cambridge Analytica scandal, which followed the revelation that the data of millions of Facebook users was breached and used by a political consulting firm.

Just two days after Zuckerberg's keynote at Meta Connect, another New Mexico jury found Meta lied about how Facebook used personal information. (The company has said it disagrees with the verdict and will defend itself against what it says are efforts to distort its record.)

So are customers willing to hand over that data for the convenience of using Muse?

Some users say yes. Since its launch one month ago, Muse already has more than five million downloads and more than three million weekly active users - outpacing the adoption of ChatGPT when that was first introduced, in the North American market.

Zuckerberg has laid out a vision in which Muse couples with an ever-expanding line-up of Meta AI smart glasses, enabling users to summon hands-free what he calls "personal superintelligence".

Meta clearly has big plans for its smart glasses. "I think they're making an investment to position themselves as a category leader," says Kate Winick, principal analyst at Forrester, covering social media and influencers. "However big this category turns out to be, they will own it - for now."

The glasses are divisive, and have been labelled by some as "pervert glasses" because they can be used to film covertly. The company has moved to stop users from tampering with the light that indicates a photo or video is being captured. Zuckerberg also just announced new audio-only smart glasses, an apparent bid to quell privacy concerns.

"Consumers know that Meta has problems, and that to date we haven't been able to trust them to make their products safe for children. So why would a consumer want to trust them with some of their most private and sensitive information?" says Brooke Istook of the Heat Initiative, a campaign group.

In his speech, Zuckerberg briefly addressed the sensitive issue of privacy. At one point during his talk, an image flashed on the screen behind him of its Muse mascot embracing a blue padlock.

items.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
items.summary: Vitalii Zhykovych gives his own account of the attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev.
items.content:
A former Ukrainian security services officer linked to a bomb attack in Monaco in June that targeted a multi-millionaire says he believed it was ordered by senior members of HUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency.

In an exclusive interview with the BBC from prison in Kyiv, facilitated by his lawyer, Vitalii Zhykovych has given his own account of the attempted assassination for the first time.

Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev and his 13-year-old son were badly hurt in the blast and his partner suffered catastrophic injuries. Yermolayev later described their survival as "nothing short of a miracle".

Zhykovych describes himself as a "freelancer" for Ukraine's SBU security service and says Anastasia Berezovska, the woman caught on camera planting the bomb in Monaco, was his "agent".

A week after the bombing, Berezovska's body was discovered in the woods west of Kyiv with gunshot wounds to the head.

But Zhykovych insists he did not send her to kill, and nor did he kill her.

He was arrested and accused of her murder together with an active-duty intelligence officer from HUR called Vladyslav Reut.

Reut initially confessed to investigators, and led them to the shallow grave. But days later in court, he changed his testimony to blame Zhykovych.

Ukrainian agent accused of murdering Monaco bomb suspect changes story

Now, responding to questions from the BBC, he alleges that Reut - who he refers to as "The Boss" - had "proposed the operation" in Monaco against Vadym Yermolayev.

"As Reut informed me, this operation […] had been authorised and approved by Reut's superiors, who served in the Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defence [HUR]," he says.

Distancing himself from the explosion itself, he alleges that Reut asked to use Berezovska for the bombing and when Zhykovych refused – he says she was not fully trained – Reut agreed to send her for reconnaissance instead.

Reut then communicated directly with Bereszovska without including him, according to Zhykovych, who alleges that Reut also provided her with the explosives.

The BBC asked HUR to comment on the latest claims. The agency has previously said that it is "committed to a full investigation" and providing "comprehensive support" to law enforcement bodies.

The SBU has described Zhykovych in a statement only as a "former law enforcement officer".

Yermolayev was attacked in Monaco as he and his family were returning from an evening meal on the seafront. A surveillance video shows Berezovska walking slightly in front of the group, then leaving the device in a bag on their doorstep.

It detonates just as they get close, apparently shocking even Berezovska with its force.

Yermolayev later said he believed that serving HUR officers, "individuals close to the agency's current and former leadership", were linked to the attack.

Berezovska was quickly identified as the suspected bomber and on 2 July her image, taken from CCTV footage, was circulated by Interpol.

She had already fled, first driving through Italy and Germany, then taking a bus from Frankfurt to Ukraine.

Before she could be caught and questioned though, she was driven to the woods by Reut and Zhykovych and killed. Each blames the other for her shooting.

The shocking case has prompted intense speculation, including over who may have wanted Yermolayev dead and why, and whether this could have been a state-ordered assassination attempt, a rogue operation or some kind of criminal score-settling.

The businessman himself, who renounced his Ukrainian passport some years ago and now has Cypriot citizenship, has dismissed multiple theories.

They include the idea the attack might be linked to a struggle between organised crime groups involved in highly lucrative scam call-centres in Ukraine.

Earlier this year, a court in Estonia convicted Yermolayev's son, Artur, of defrauding its citizens out of millions of euros through such "offisy", as the scam networks are known in Ukraine.

Vadym Yermolayev told the Ukrainska Pravda newspaper that he "never had anything to do with anything" in the case.

He alleges that Reut told him the bombing was in retaliation for "funding the annexation of Crimea", which he understood to mean Yermolayev was paying taxes to Russia from businesses in Russian-occupied Crimea.

"In my view, this constitutes grounds for the operation," he communicated from prison.

Yermolayev has repeatedly denied any remaining business interests linked to Russia.

At his most recent custody hearing in Kyiv, surrounded by heavily armed guards, Zhykovych spoke publicly for the first time since his arrest. The BBC were the only media present.

At one point Zhykovych said Reut had in fact told him the attack in Monaco was not "authorised".

"Someone had ordered this target from the civilian side," Zhykovych said, without explaining.

The judge then interrupted, reminding him that he was addressing an open court.

Zhykovych also revealed that Reut originally talked of two targets.

When we asked, he said he could not disclose the second name. Other sources strongly suggest it was a pro-Russian blogger tried and convicted in absentia last year by Ukraine of treason.

As the investigation continues – into both the bombing in Monaco and the murder in Ukraine - Berezovska's family have many questions of their own.

The 39-year-old had been in Germany since early 2022, when she left Ukraine as a refugee with her young son.

Zhykovych now claims she was living a double-life, working with him as an agent "against Muscovy" – meaning Russia.

He said they had met online and told us the pair were working to "repel the armed aggression of the Russian Federation".

Berezovska's husband has told the BBC that the allegation was "nonsense". He believes she was dragged, unwittingly, into the whole affair.

Zhykovych says Berezovska called him the day after the Monaco attack, and when he asked why she had done it, she said Reut had promised her a huge fee. "$50,000 doesn't just lie on the streets," she supposedly explained.

Residents in her village have told us that Berezovska was saving to buy a flat. But when she travelled to Ukraine to collect the money, she was lured into the woods and shot.

Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko and Volodymyr Lozhko.

items.title: Dombrovskis sulla flessibilità: “Le regole attuali già aiutano”. Si tratta sulla lettera di Roma
items.summary: Il commissario: “Al vaglio la proposta italiana, parlato con Giorgetti”. Scontro fra frugali e paesi del Sud. Ok alla clausola di salvaguardia
items.content:
LUSSEMBURGO – La Commissione ha valutato positivamente le richieste di Grecia e Italia di avvalersi di questa maggiore flessibilità. Le esamineremo più a fondo». I costi dell’energia e lo shock inflazionistico è stato al centro della riunione dell’Eurogruppo (i ministri finanziari che hanno adottato l’euro) svoltasi ieri in Lussemburgo. E il Commissario agli Affari economici, Valdis Dombrovskis, non ha chiuso la porta alla proposta di Roma e Atene. Mentre è stata bocciata con nettezza l’idea di utilizzare l’extragettito Iva, determinato dal rialzo dei prezzi, per abbassare i prezzi dei carburanti.

«Il quadro delle regole fiscali – ha ricordato Dombrovskis che ha avuto un colloquio con il ministro italiano, Giancarlo Giorgetti - contiene già elementi che aiutano e tengono conto della questione dell’aumento dell’inflazione e dell’impatto di una maggiore inflazione» ma «siamo pronti a proporre misure di risposta, se necessario». L’esecutivo europeo teme che venga distolta l’attenzione dalla sostenibilità dei conti pubblici e nello stesso tempo non può sottovalutare la necessità di aiutare i soggetti più deboli dinanzi al probabile ulteriore rialzo dell’inflazione. Per questo Dombrovskis ha anche avvertito che non si può «continuare a introdurre nuove forme di flessibilità fiscale». Come ha sintetizzato il presidente dell’Eurogruppo, il greco Kiriakou Pierrakakis, bisogna «proteggere senza dare segnali sbagliati sulle politiche di bilancio». «Siamo fiduciosi – ha detto con un pizzico di soddisfazione Giorgetti che ha incassato il via libera della Commissione alla clausola di salvaguardia per la difesa e l’energia che consentirà di spendere 28 miliardi nei prossimi due anni - che le buone ragioni tecniche potranno, con gli opportuni approfondimenti e le adeguate forme, trovare la corretta interpretazione delle regole con decisioni coerenti con la sostenibilità della finanza pubblica».

Come al solito, però, il tema ha riproposto il solito confronto tra i cosiddetti paesi “frugali” e i “flessibili” . La Spagna, attraverso il suo ministro Carlos Cuerpo , ha aperto alle richieste italo-greche: «Siamo pronti a prenderle in considerazione. Dobbiamo essere consapevoli delle circostanze eccezionali». L’Olanda, con il Belgio, ha invece alzato le barricate. «Comincio a essere piuttosto stanco di questa discussione – ha stigmatizzato Eelco Heinen -. Ogni volta che si presenta un problema sento sempre la stessa cosa: modifichiamo le regole fiscali». Un po’ meno critico il tedesco Lars Klingbeil il quale ha ricordato che «le regole fiscali europee sono state appena riviste, ma la Commissione europea deve affrontare le questioni che preoccupano i cittadini, e cioè gli elevati prezzi dell’energia». E sul piatto ha messo la tassa sugli extraprofitti delle società energetiche.

«Nel breve termine – ha quindi annunciato il presidente del consiglio europeo, Antonio Costa, riferendosi al summit della prossima settimana - dobbiamo fornire indicazioni alla Commissione in merito a misure mirate e temporanee volte ad attenuare l’impatto dei prezzi elevati dell ’energia». Segno che lo scontro sulla flessibilità si trasferirà anche sul tavolo dei capi di Stato e di Governo.

items.title: What Americans think about the death penalty
items.summary: The BBC spoke to Americans and international tourists in Washington DC about their views on the death penalty following the botched execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee.
items.content:
Christa Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September. Experts described it as unprecedented.

The failure of Pike's execution has reignited the debate about capital punishment and its use in the United States.

The BBC spoke to Americans as well as international tourists in Washington DC about their views on the death penalty.

items.title: I sindacati: 'Da lunedì sciopero nazionale ex Ilva di 24 ore'
items.summary: Dopo l'incontro a Palazzo Chigi
items.content:
Da lunedi proclamate 24 ore di sciopero nazionale in tutti gli stabilimenti Ex Ilva. Lo hanno annunciato i sindacati alla fine del tavolo a Palazzo Chigi con il governo

Una doccia gelata per l'ex Ilva. Acciaierie d'Italia ha annunciato uno stop agli impianti di Taranto, Genova e Novi Ligure nello stesso giorno dell'incontro a Palazzo Chigi tra governo e sindacati sul futuro dell'azienda. Nel corso del tavolo il sottosegretario alla Presidenza del Consiglio, Alfredo Mantovano , ha indicato che il governo intende portare nel prossimo Consiglio dei ministri un decreto-legge che contenga le tutele sociali per i lavoratori e che punti a una Cassa integrazione non per chiusura attività, ma in una prospettiva di continuità. L'obiettivo del governo è una produzione di acciaio green con impianto Dri e forni elettrici, purché nell'ambito di un piano industriale credibile, ha spiegato il sottosegretario.

Intanto a partire da domani, 9 ottobre, saranno sospese tutte le attività produttive degli impianti dell'area a caldo dello stabilimento ex Ilva di Taranto, afferma Acciaierie d'Italia in As, in una nota inviata a prefetto, enti locali e forze dell'ordine. La decisione viene ricondotta all'ottemperanza al decreto della Corte d'Appello di Milano del 27 luglio , dopo il rigetto, notificato il 5 ottobre , della richiesta di sospensione dell'esecuzione. L'azienda fa anche richiesta di ammortizzatori sociali. Gli impianti saranno mantenuti in modalità di riscaldo, "hot stand-by", in attesa della decisione della Corte di Cassazione. Ma "in assenza" di un provvedimento favorevole, il 24 ottobre verrà "sospeso" anche il mantenimento in riscaldo , con lo spegnimento definitivo dell'area a caldo entro il 25 ottobre , "senza alcuna possibilità" di riavvio successivo.

items.title: Il corteo per ricordare Maricarmen Abascal
items.summary: Cioè la donna di 87 anni per cui erano cominciate le proteste contro gli sfratti in Spagna: giovedì sera a Madrid c'erano circa 20mila persone
items.content:
Giovedì sera a Madrid circa 20mila persone hanno partecipato a un lungo corteo in ricordo di María del Carmen Abascal , la donna per cui erano partite le grandi proteste contro la crisi abitativa in Spagna, morta in ospedale mercoledì. Abascal aveva 87 anni, era conosciuta come Maricarmen e lo scorso 23 settembre era stata sfrattata dal suo appartamento in centro città in cui aveva vissuto la gran parte della sua vita. Le cause della sua morte non sono note.

Il corteo che passa dalla Puerta de Alcalá a Madrid, giovedì sera (Richard Zubelzu/ZUMA Press Wire via ANSA)

La manifestazione è partita dalla Puerta del Sol, la piazza principale di Madrid, dove da giorni alcuni manifestanti si sono accampati con delle tende, e si è diretta verso calle del Alcalde Sainz de Baranda, la via in cui viveva la donna, circa 3,5 chilometri più a est. A guidarla sono stati i membri del Sindacato delle inquiline, che indossavano gilet arancioni catarifrangenti e portavano una corona di fiori con la scritta «Continueremo a lottare per te».

Una volta arrivati davanti a casa della donna, i manifestanti hanno osservato un minuto di silenzio. Alcuni hanno acceso le torce degli smartphone. Alla fine il silenzio è stato interrotto da una serie di applausi e cori.

In queste settimane Abascal era diventata il simbolo di un problema assai diffuso nelle grandi città spagnole: quello degli inquilini di lungo corso che faticano a pagare affitti sempre più alti, così alti da superare perfino l’importo medio di uno stipendio o di una pensione. Subito dopo lo sfratto la donna era stata ricoverata in ospedale per gli effetti dell’ansia e dello stress (aveva peraltro un’invalidità riconosciuta del 50 per cento). Dopo le prime proteste, i suoi legali e i familiari avevano fatto un accordo con i proprietari dell’immobile per farla tornare a casa.

Le persone che partecipano al corteo con le torce degli smartphone accese (REUTERS/Susana Vera)

Per tentare di placare le proteste e soddisfare alcune richieste dei manifestanti il governo del primo ministro socialista Pedro Sánchez aveva approvato due decreti sulla crisi abitativa, che però erano stati bocciati dal parlamento. La bocciatura ha portato Sánchez a indire elezioni anticipate per il prossimo 29 novembre. Il governo spagnolo comunque ha approvato con qualche modifica due nuovi decreti , contando di riuscire a convertirli infine in legge.

Un uomo mostra una foto di Maricarmen Abascal prima dell’inizio del corteo (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez)

items.title: AI-ready biological data: $1.8B global commitment
items.summary: Article URL: https://biohub.org/news/virtual-biology-initiative-expansion/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50011999 Points: 105 # Comments: 14
items.content:
REDWOOD CITY, CA, October 7, 2026 — Biohub, the U.S. Department of Energy, the National Institutes of Health, and new funding partners today announced a major expansion of an international effort to generate and make accessible the data enabling predictive AI models of biology. Together, the organizations are investing $1.8 billion in funding, data, computation, and new measurement technology, the largest coordinated commitment to generating AI-ready biological data to date. The result will be an open resource for the research community that provides the foundation for greater understanding and ultimately treatment of human diseases.

As part of this announcement, Biohub has partnered with the Department of Energy (DOE) Office of Science and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to advance the frontier of artificial intelligence in biology. DOE will invest more than $500 million over five years in lab measurement, modeling and computation toward the international effort to build an AI-ready open data resource. NIH will coordinate the contribution of relevant datasets, repositories, and knowledge bases developed through more than $500 million in prior federal investment aligned to this initiative. Biohub will work with NIH to standardize these datasets for AI model training.

In addition, Google DeepMind, Isomorphic Labs, and Meta are collectively investing $300 million in the Virtual Biology Initiative to create the technologies and multi-modal datasets needed to build predictive models of life.

These datasets will enable the global scientific community to collectively build and use AI models that allow researchers to ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally, accelerating the path to new ways of preventing and treating diseases. This initiative will deliver the foundational measurements to train these models, expanding cell response data to interventions across far more cell types and conditions than have yet been studied, and building and validating technologies for studying cells and cellular interactions at greater scale, speed, and accuracy.

“An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally. The insights that come from this could unlock a far greater understanding of disease and open up completely new paths for cures,” said Biohub Head of Science Alex Rives. “Because of this potential, the creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together. We invite the worldwide scientific community to join us in this project.”

The Virtual Biology Initiative, announced in April 2026, will coordinate data generation across institutions and disciplines to build AI-ready open datasets to enable predictive models of life. Biohub’s founding $500 million commitment anchors that work: $400 million supports new technologies that expand what biologists can measure: cryo-electron tomography, which resolves near-atomic detail inside the cell; microscopy that can image millions to billions of cells in living tissue; and engineering tools to build and perturb biology at molecular, cellular, tissue, and whole-organism levels. A further $100 million funds research outside Biohub.

“Generating the data to solve predictive systems biology requires scaling past the limits of what any single organization can produce today,” said Max Jaderberg, President of Isomorphic Labs. “By joining the Virtual Biology Initiative as a founding member, Isomorphic Labs is helping build a massive, multimodal data foundation. This initiative will generate the data needed to push the industry closer to the next significant breakthrough for biology.”

Through the Genesis Mission, a cross-agency initiative led by the Department of Energy, DOE will contribute more than $500 million over five years in fundamental cell research — data collection, AI analytics, measurement and imaging, modeling, and computation — drawing on exascale supercomputing, X-ray and neutron scattering, cryo-electron microscopy and tomography, and autonomous laboratories across the National Laboratory system.

“This partnership represents a critical step forward in leveraging artificial intelligence for public benefit,” said Darío Gil, DOE’s Under Secretary for Science. “By combining DOE’s exascale computing, experimental measurement, and modeling assets, including premier user facilities at the Joint Genome Institute, the Environmental Molecular Sciences Laboratory, and advanced structural beamlines with the unique AI models, tool development, and biological data capabilities of Biohub, we are setting a new standard for open science that will accelerate discoveries in both medicine and biotechnology.”

Through its Bio Genesis Mission , NIH will bring together existing biomedical datasets, national data infrastructure, and research programs to help build AI-ready resources for the broader scientific community. NIH’s extensive investments in biomedical research provide a foundation for this work; resources include national biomedical repositories catalogued by NIH’s National Library of Medicine (NLM) and the National Center for Biotechnology Information , as well as NIH Common Fund programs that are already developing coordinated biological atlases, shared data standards, and AI-ready biomedical datasets.

“By combining resources and expertise, we can accelerate the development of universal cell models with sufficient biological complexity to predict how any cell responds to an intervention,” said Nicole Kleinstreuer, Ph.D., NIH Deputy Director Program Coordination, Planning, and Strategic Initiatives (DPCPSI). “The return from these models could be broad and profound, resulting in substantially faster timelines for medical breakthroughs as compared with attempting to attain the same results through laboratory experiments alone.”

In addition, leading scientific institutions and consortia with experience in organizing transformative international collaborations, from the Human Genome Project onwards, have come together to help nucleate the scientific community across academia and industry around developing effective scientific strategies to maximize the impact of virtual biology. The groups include the Allen Institute, Broad Institute, Gladstone Institutes, the Human Cell Atlas, the Human Protein Atlas, and the Wellcome Sanger Institute. These groups are committed to working together as part of the Virtual Biology Initiative as well as through independent efforts toward this shared goal. NVIDIA will support the initiative to leverage accelerated computing infrastructure, domain-specific software, and technical expertise. Renaissance Philanthropy is helping to expand funding for data generation.

As the initiative takes shape, Biohub is bringing together partners across disciplines and industries to build the layer that lets their datasets work in a unified fashion — shared standards, common identifiers, and a single point of access. Equally important is building the scientific community around these resources — convening researchers across institutions and disciplines, connecting complementary expertise and capabilities, and creating opportunities to define and pursue ambitious scientific questions together. Over the past decade, Biohub has expanded the reach and impact of measurement technologies and open datasets, leading projects such as Tabula Sapiens , OpenCell , and Zebrahub . It has also built and maintained community data infrastructure, including CELLxGENE and the CryoET Data Portal . The Virtual Biology Initiative builds on these experiences to enable coordinated efforts at a scale that no single institution could achieve alone.

“The quest to build a virtual cell is one of the great collective scientific challenges and key to understanding the mechanisms of life. We will not solve this challenge without open, experimental biological data at an unprecedented scale, showing how living cells behave and respond to changes,” said Pushmeet Kohli, VP, AI for Science at Google DeepMind and Google Cloud’s Chief Scientist. “This investment in biological data generation will help create an open, standardized data commons, which will lay the foundations researchers around the world need to better model biology.”

About Biohub Biohub is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research institute combining frontier AI and biology to accelerate science. With its compute capacity, AI research and engineering, and state-of-the-art technology for measuring, imaging, and programming biology, Biohub is enabling scientists worldwide to use AI-powered biology to study how cells operate and organize as systems — with the ultimate mission to cure or prevent all disease. Learn more at biohub.org .

items.title: ADHD as a circadian rhythm disorder: evidence and implications for chronotherapy (2025)
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1697900/full Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50011928 Points: 262 # Comments: 153
items.content:
Volume 16 - 2025 | https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1697900

1. Department of Respirology, Queens University, Kingston, ON, Canada

2. University of Ottawa, Department of Psychiatry, Ottawa, ON, Canada

Accumulating evidence indicates that circadian rhythm dysfunction is a clinically significant and highly prevalent phenotype in a substantial subgroup of individuals with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). This perspective synthesizes convergent lines of evidence demonstrating strong associations between ADHD and evening chronotype with phase-delayed biological markers. Sleep disturbances are profound: insomnia and sleep disturbances affect up to 80% of adults with ADHD and similarly up to 82% of children with ADHD, delayed sleep-wake timing occurs in up to 78%, and dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) is delayed by approximately 45 minutes in children and 90 minutes in adults. These alterations coincide with blunted and delayed cortisol rhythms, reduced pineal volume, and attenuated peripheral clock-gene rhythms (BMAL1/PER2). Intervention studies demonstrate that the circadian phase can be successfully advanced in ADHD populations. Melatonin and bright light therapy has advanced DLMO in both children and adults with ADHD. Emerging data correlate phase advancement with ADHD symptom improvement, and winter trials suggest circadian preference shifts best predict symptom improvement. Sleep programs improve ADHD symptoms, sleep quality, and functioning in children. Exercise and multimodal protocols for evening chronotypes successfully advance circadian timing in non-ADHD populations and warrant investigation in ADHD. Based on this evidence, we propose a pragmatic, behavioral-first clinical pathway: routine screening for sleep/circadian disturbances; phenotypic characterization through chronotype assessment, sleep tracking, and DLMO when feasible; implementation of fixed wake times, morning bright light exposure, evening light restriction with screen hygiene, and regularized zeitgebers; and selective low-dose melatonin for confirmed or probable DLMO delays.

Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by impaired levels of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity ( 1 ). There is a growing body of research identifying that ADHD has a significant sleep and circadian component ( 2 , 3 ). Insomnia is present in up to 80% of adults with ADHD and similarly high rates (up to 82%) of children with ADHD ( 4 , 5 ). Converging evidence indicates that circadian rhythm disruption represents a highly prevalent and clinically important phenotype that interacts with ADHD symptoms in complex, bidirectional ways in a substantial proportion (though not all) of individuals. In parallel, clinical trials have begun targeting the circadian system and have demonstrated that phase shifting the internal clock of people with ADHD can improve symptoms.

Herein, we propose the adoption of behavioral circadian interventions as adjuncts in ADHD care. This circadian-informed approach is a pragmatic, scalable, and generally low risk. We invite rigorously future well-designed, stratified trials to quantify effects on core ADHD outcomes, define responder phenotypes, and optimize circadian-focused protocols.

An estimated 73-78% of children and adults with ADHD have a delayed sleep/wake cycle ( 6 ). These findings persist even in the absence of comorbid mental health conditions, with multiple independent studies confirming elevated rates of self-reported sleep problems in adults with ADHD ( 7 ). These subjective reports are corroborated by objective sleep studies, which demonstrate that sleep onset latency and sleep efficiency problems remain significantly associated with ADHD even after controlling for anxiety and depression ( 8 ).

A comprehensive systematic review found robust evidence for evening chronotype predominance in ADHD ( 2 ). Approximately three-quarters of adults who developed ADHD in childhood show objective evidence of phase-delayed circadian rhythms. Biological markers such as dim-light melatonin onset in saliva, core body temperature rhythms, and actigraphically-recorded sleep patterns are typically shifted later by roughly 90 minutes compared to neurotypical adults ( 9 ).

Phase delays of melatonin in both individuals with ADHD have been well characterized, with children and adults identified to have a delayed onset of about 45 minutes and 90 minutes, respectively ( 10 ). Beyond the phase delay of melatonin onset in ADHD, there is evidence that the amount and pattern of melatonin production may differ ( Figure 1 ). Some studies have observed abnormally high levels of melatonin during the day in children with ADHD, which improves with methylphenidate treatment ( 6 ). This ability to suppress daytime melatonin levels and shift the melatonin rhythm earlier suggests a complex interplay between ADHD medications and circadian systems. Individuals with ADHD have also been found to have smaller pineal gland (which produces and secretes melatonin) volume compared to healthy controls, with a positive correlation between pineal gland volume and eveningness ( 11 ).

ADHD also involves blunted and delayed cortisol rhythms ( Figure 1 ) ( 12 , 13 ). In an analysis of adults with ADHD compared to age- and sex-matched controls, adults with ADHD had significantly disturbed rhythmicity of not only melatonin but cortisol ( 12 ). A meta-analysis also identified that children with ADHD exhibit lower basal cortisol levels, particularly in the morning, compared to controls ( 13 ). This suggests a deficit in the suprachiasmatic nucleus’ ability to entrain a normal circadian rhythm with alterations in the circadian rhythm expanding past melatonin. However, the causation of this is still unclear, as it has been postulated that more eveningness and thus light exposure could also be driving these findings.

Brain and Muscle ARNT-like 1 (BMAL1) and Period circadian protein homolog 2 (PER2) are core components of the circadian clock in humans, which form a feedback loop to control gene expression in a cyclical manner. Downstream, attenuated BMAL1/PER2 rhythms in oral mucosa indicate weaker or desynchronized peripheral clocks, and symptom severity tracks with reduced PER2 rhythmicity, tying molecular clock strength to the clinical phenotype ( 12 ). Together, these data support a model in which individuals with ADHD consistently experience shifted endocrine signals (melatonin/cortisol) coupled with molecular disruptions via the loss of the rhythmic expression of clock genes.

In a randomized trial of adults with ADHD, 0.5 mg per night of melatonin advanced DLMO by 88 minutes with 14% reduction in ADHD symptoms ( 14 ). In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 101 medication-free children with ADHD and chronic sleep-onset insomnia, 3–6 mg melatonin nightly for 4 weeks advanced DLMO by 44 minutes, while the control group had a delay of 13 minutes. Total sleep time also significantly improved by 20 minutes with melatonin, versus a loss of 14 minutes in the control group. However, within this 4 week period, there was no identified changes in cognitive performance or problem behavior ( 15 ). In a long-term follow up study of this cohort, 65% of participants continued daily melatonin; discontinuation resulted in a phase delay of sleep in 92% of children ( 16 ). Positive improvements in behavior (71%) and mood (61%) were reported. Altogether, these findings suggest melatonin effectively advances circadian phase in ADHD; however, further trials are needed to define optimal dose and timing relative to DLMO, the duration required for sleep/phase gains to translate into core symptom improvement, and responder phenotypes.

Studies in healthy populations have demonstrated a powerful ability to phase advance DLMO using bright light exposure. A week of natural light-dark cycle was able to entrain a ~2.6h earlier DLMO in healthy adults ( 17 ). Emerging research indicates that morning bright light can help stabilize sleep and circadian rhythms in ADHD ( 14 , 18 , 19 ). Adding bright light therapy to melatonin yielded the largest phase advance (~2 hours) in adults with ADHD and delayed sleep phase ( 14 ). In another pilot trial, 2 weeks of morning bright light therapy with a 10,000 lux lamp phase advanced DLMO by 31 minutes and mid-sleep time by 57 minutes in adults with ADHD. There was a significant interaction between ADHD-Rating Scales and Hyperactive-Impulsive sub-scores with phase advances in DLMO and mid-sleep time ( 18 ).

A 3-week intervention examined the role of bright light therapy in adults with ADHD during the fall/winter period ( 19 ). Phase advance in circadian preference emerged as the strongest independent predictor of improvement across subjective and objective ADHD indices. These findings, especially in the winter period, are especially relevant as there is a strong relationship between ADHD symptoms and symptoms of seasonal depression ( 20 ). One analysis suggested that circadian disturbance significantly mediated the relationship between ADHD and seasonal symptoms of depression ( 20 ). In clinical populations, the overall rate of seasonal affective disorder is 27% among adults with ADHD, with females at the highest risk ( 21 ). While more trials are required, bright light therapy may be even more efficacious for individuals with ADHD during winter months ( 20 ).

items.title: Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar dies suddenly at 75
items.summary: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.
items.content:
Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar, known for his intense, fiery performances on stage and in film, has died at the age of 75 in Goa.

One of the most recognisable faces of Indian cinema, Patekar won three National Film Awards and became known for playing difficult and often volatile characters. He was also a prominent figure in Marathi language cinema and theatre.

He was admitted to a hospital after being found unconscious at his home in Goa in the early hours of Thursday.

"Despite 45 minutes of continuous CPR, he could not be revived," Dr Shekhar Salkar of Manipal Hospital in Goa told ANI news agency. Tributes have poured in from actors and politicians across India.

Dr Salkar later told PTI news agency that the hospital team found Patekar at his home "unconscious and almost unresponsive".

The team continued giving him CPR even while taking him to the hospital, located about 10 minutes away, but he was dead by the time they reached there, he added.

Dr Salkar said Patekar had suffered a cardiac arrest, but it was not clear what had triggered it.

Family, friends and fans paid their last respects to the actor at Goa Medical College, ahead of his funeral which was to take place later in the day with full state honours at his farm house in the western city of Pune in Maharashtra state.

In the evening, his remains were flown to Pune by air ambulance, where the state's chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis paid his last respects, before Patekar's body was taken to his farm in Donje village where last rites were performed and he was cremated.

Times of India reports that his son, Malhar, told reporters afterwards that his father has not truly gone anywhere and will to remain with them - even if not physically - and his commitment to social welfare would live on.

Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi led tributes to the actor, praising Patekar's versatility and outspoken personality.

Patekar portrayed characters that would "remain etched in the memory of generations", Modi wrote on X, adding that his death had left "a vast void in the artistic world".

Bollywood veteran Anupam Kher paid tribute to his friend on social media, saying he would miss his warmth and extraordinary performances and called him "one of the finest actors and human beings in Indian cinema".

Another Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan called him "a mentor, a teacher, a critic and a friend", adding that Patekar has "left a void not only in the world of cinema but in the hearts of all Indians and the world".

Akshay Kumar, who appeared alongside Patekar in the comedy film Welcome, remembered him as a rare performer whose voice, intensity and honesty could command an audience's attention.

Patekar made his debut with the film Gaman in 1978 and continued to play smaller roles in several films. But the intensity that he brought on the screen was hard to miss and soon he landed a role in Parinda in 1989, making him a household name across India. He won his first National Film Award and the Filmfare Award as well for his portrayal of the gangster Anna in the film.

He didn't look back after this and portrayed many memorable roles in films in the 1990s. The range of characters he played showcased the depth of his acting talent and mastery of his craft.

Famous dialogues from his films, delivered in his inimitable rasping voice, were quoted in school corridors and tea stalls. Many professional comedians imitate his distinctive style even today.

"He had a distinctive style of working and how he approached characters. As a person, he was outspoken and difficult to get along with but directors would still want to work with him because he was simply a fantastic actor," film trade analyst Komal Nahta told BBC.

His portrayal of Major Chauhan in Prahaar – a film he also directed – won him praise. His other characters, including the patriotic hero of Tirangaa and Pratap Narayan Tilak in Krantiveer, also won him accolades.

Just when critics thought that playing loud characters was his mainstay, he proved them wrong by delivering a mesmerising performance in Khamoshi as a person who could not hear or speak.

Director Prakash Jha's Rajneeti in 2010 added another dimension to his acting as his portrayal of an astute politician was delivered with perfection.

The breadth of Patekar's career showcases the wide range of his work. He played different but contrasting roles like that of a notorious gangster or a policeman with equal ease. He also sometimes worked behind the camera as a director and writer.

His three national awards for Parinda, Krantiveer and Agni Sakshi are testament to his wide-ranging career.

Patekar was an influential figure too in both Marathi and Hindi theatre. Before making his debut in films, he was involved in theatre, where he developed his gritty style of dialogue delivery and also mastered the intensity he brought to his on-screen characters.

Purush and Hamidabai Chi Kothi were two of his most famous plays. Despite being successful in films, he remained active in theatre throughout his professional life.

Patekar was known for his activism and didn't mince his words while criticising the government of the day. He was direct, and almost brazen and unapologetic, when it came to criticising ministers and their policies - and did so quite publicly.

Issues related to farmers were particularly close to his heart.

His work went beyond just giving statements. In 2015 he and actor Makarand Anaspure established the Naam Foundation, which has worked on farmer welfare and water conservation in Maharashtra.

In 2018, allegations of sexual harassment made by actor Tanushree Dutta against Patekar over an alleged incident on a film set a decade earlier helped spark India's #MeToo movement . Patekar denied the allegations.

In 2019, he was cleared of the charges after police said they had not found sufficient evidence against him.

items.title: È morto Francesco Tedesco, storico collaboratore dell'ANSA a Napoli
items.summary: Aveva 53 anni. Malato da tempo, lascia moglie e figlia. Il cordoglio delle istituzioni e del calcio
items.content: Il mondo dell'informazione campano piange la scomparsa di Francesco Tedesco, 53 anni, napoletano, giornalista professionista e storico collaboratore dell'agenzia ANSA. Da alcuni anni combatteva contro una grave malattia alla quale aveva reagito con il coraggio del sorriso, continuando a lavorare con l'entusiasmo e la professionalità che lo avevano fatto apprezzare a diverse generazioni di colleghi. Dopo gli inizi all'agenzia Rotopress, aveva cominciato nel 2005 un lungo sodalizio lavorativo con l'ANSA nella sede di Napoli, prima nel progetto ANSAmed e poi diventando punto di riferimento per il notiziario generale specializzandosi nelle coperture di avvenimenti politici e sportivi. Alla collaborazione con l'agenzia alternava il lavoro nel settore degli uffici stampa, conquistando uguali stima e consensi come comunicatore dallo stile creativo ed efficace. Sposato e padre di una figlia, negli anni aveva costruito una solida reputazione professionale basate sull'equilibrio, l'affidabilità e le esclusive che sapeva mettere a segno, e che lo avevano fatto conoscere e apprezzare in tutte le redazioni campane. La profonda umanità e il rispetto costante per gli interlocutori erano il tratto distintivo di un approccio al lavoro che, fino agli ultimi giorni, lo ha visto segnalare eventi e notizie ai colleghi e amici dell'ANSA, che ne conserveranno un ricordo indelebile. Il sindaco di Napoli, Gaetano Manfredi, insieme a tutta la Giunta e all'Amministrazione comunale, esprime il più profondo cordoglio:. "La notizia della morte di Francesco Tedesco ci addolora profondamente. Di Francesco tutti noi abbiamo sempre apprezzato ed ammirato la straordinaria professionalità, la rigorosa preparazione e, soprattutto, la grande umanità che ha costantemente riposto nel suo lavoro e nei rapporti personali. È una grave perdita per la nostra comunità e per quanti hanno avuto il privilegio di collaborare con lui e conoscerlo da vicino". In questo momento di dolore, il sindaco, la Giunta e la città di Napoli - si conclude la nota dell'Amministrazione partenopea - si stringono con affetto e vicinanza alla famiglia, ai colleghi dell'Ansa e a tutti i suoi cari. La notizia della scomparsa di Francesco Tedesco, giovane giornalista di Ansa, ci lascia attoniti. A nome mio e del Consiglio Regionale della Campania esprimiamo profondo cordoglio e sentite condoglianze alla sua famiglia e alla redazione di Ansa Campania". E' quanto afferma il Presidente del Consiglio Regionale della Campania, Massimiliano Manfredi, che aggiunge: "Abbiamo avuto tante occasioni, in questi lunghi anni di lavoro, spesso condivisi sui rispettivi fronti della politica e del giornalismo, di apprezzare la sua professionalita', il suo impegno, la sua capacità di costruire relazioni con i colleghi basate sul rispetto e sulla solidarietà. Lo ricorderemo con grande stima ed affetto". 'La scomparsa di Francesco Tedesco mi addolora profondamente. Ho sempre stimato in lui il professionista serio, preparato e versatile, capace di raccontare la politica e la città con equilibrio e rigore. Era una persona garbata, che affrontava il lavoro e le persone con il sorriso e con una rara umanità. Ai colleghi dell'ANSA, ai tanti giornalisti campani che lo hanno conosciuto e apprezzato, alla moglie e alla figlia vanno il mio abbraccio e la mia vicinanza. Napoli perde un grande professionista e una persona perbene'. Così, in una nota, Sergio Costa, vicepresidente della Camera e deputato del M5s. "Il presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis, l'area comunicazione e tutta la Ssc Napoli esprimono profondo cordoglio per la scomparsa di Francesco Tedesco, stimato giornalista dell'ANSA che si è sempre contraddistinto per la sua correttezza, educazione ed enorme professionalità. Ai suoi familiari la nostra più sincera vicinanza". E' il messaggio di cordoglio postato sui canali ufficiali del Calcio Napoli per la notizia della morte del giornalista Francesco Tedesco, che per anni ha raccontato per l'ANSA le vicende della squadra partenopea.

items.title: La portaerei USS Lincoln è arrivata a San Diego, in California, dopo più di trecento giorni di missione
items.content:
Dopo circa dieci mesi di missione la portaerei della marina statunitense USS Abraham Lincoln è arrivata a San Diego, in California. La Lincoln aveva lasciato la città nel novembre del 2025 e da mesi si trovava in Medio Oriente, dove ha preso parte alla guerra contro l’Iran. La nave ha passato in mare un periodo eccezionalmente lungo, e questo ha causato numerosi problemi logistici. Le notizie emerse sulle condizioni dell’equipaggio avevano descritto diversi problemi a bordo: scarsità di cibo, guasti alle tubature e numerosi casi di disagio psicologico tra i marinai, fra cui alcuni tentativi di suicidio.

Durante i mesi in missione la portaerei aveva attraccato solo tre volte: un mese dopo la partenza nella base statunitense di Guam, durante il viaggio di ritorno, per cinque giorni a Pattaya, in Thailandia , e poi di nuovo per un giorno a Guam. La USS Lincoln ha quindi passato 322 giorni in missione: per una portaerei statunitense è il secondo dispiegamento più lungo dai tempi della guerra in Vietnam (il record è detenuto dalla USS Gerald R. Ford, segnato a maggio del 2026 con 327 giorni).

Mercoledì 7 ottobre, il segretario della Difesa statunitense Pete Hegseth è volato a bordo della USS Lincoln, e ha conferito all’equipaggio la Presidential Unit Citation , la più alta onorificenza che può essere data a un’unità della marina militare statunitense.

items.title: La Ue: 'Esaminiamo le richieste dell'Italia sulla flessibilità ma serve prudenza'
items.summary: Giorgetti: 'Fiduciosi di corretta interpretazione'. Primo ok a clausola italiana
items.content:
La Commissione Ue esaminerà più a fondo le richieste italiane di flessibilità fiscale per fronteggiare l'inflazione, ma invita intanto alla prudenza e al rispetto dei piani di spesa concordati con Bruxelles. Da parte sua il ministro dell'Economia Giancarlo Giorgetti si dice fiducioso che le ragioni italiane troveranno spazio nell'interpretazione delle regole. Intanto l'Italia incassa il primo via libera di Bruxelles alla clausola di salvaguardia nazionale per energia e difesa. Dai Paesi 'frugali' e non solo, Olanda e Belgio su tutti, è arrivato intanto un chiaro altolà alla richieste di nuova flessibilità. "Esamineremo più a fondo le richieste di Italia e Grecia.

Oggi ho avuto colloqui sia con il ministro greco Kyriakos Pierrakakis sia con il ministro Giorgetti per discutere della situazione", ha spiegato il commissario europeo Valdis Dombrovskis. "Il quadro delle regole fiscali contiene già elementi che aiutano e tengono conto della questione dell'aumento dell'inflazione e dell'impatto di una maggiore inflazione sulla traiettoria di crescita della spesa netta", ha sottolineato. Tra le turbolenze sui mercati obbligazionari globali e gli spread al rialzo nell'eurozona "è necessaria prudenza fiscale". "Gli Stati membri dovrebbero attenersi agli obiettivi dei piani strutturali di bilancio a medio termine e utilizzare con cautela la flessibilità disponibile nell'ambito della clausola di salvaguardia nazionale", ha quindi avvertito. Il nuovo quadro fiscale, ha ricordato, "contiene già diversi elementi di flessibilità per affrontare la situazione attuale in modo equilibrato", "non possiamo continuare a introdurre nuove forme di flessibilità fiscale".

Dombrovskis non ha fatto alcun riferimento all'ipotesi di Roma di non usare l'extragettito fiscale legato all'inflazione solo per ridurre il debito. Ha però avvertito le regole del Patto sono anticicliche e anche grazie a questo "un aumento della spesa per interessi non deve essere compensato" nel piano di spesa. Giorgetti, dal canto suo, ha riferito di un "ampio dibattito sulle ricadute negative sui conti pubblici causate dall'inflazione", nel quale la proposta italiana "ha ricevuto numerosi consensi, al netto delle tradizionali perplessità dei Paesi 'frugali'". "Alla Commissione abbiamo chiesto un'ulteriore riflessione sulla questione al fine di una corretta interpretazione dei fattori rilevanti per il rispetto dell'attuale Patto di stabilità", ha spiegato.

"Siamo fiduciosi che le buone ragioni tecniche potranno, con gli opportuni approfondimenti e le adeguate forme, trovare la corretta interpretazione delle regole anche all'interno della clausola energia già approvata con decisioni coerenti con la sostenibilità della finanza pubblica". Sul fronte della clausola di salvaguardia nazionale (Nec), la Commissione ha intanto concluso positivamente la valutazione della richiesta italiana, presentata l'11 settembre, ritenendo che non metta a rischio la sostenibilità dei conti pubblici nel medio termine. Il fascicolo passa ora al Consiglio, che avrà un mese per dare il via libera definitivo attivando la clausola. Nelle intenzioni del governo, la Nec dovrebbe consentire all'Italia di utilizzare margini di bilancio fino all'1,5% del Pil complessivamente, pari a circa 35 miliardi di euro, tra il 2027 e il 2028: circa 14 miliardi per misure energetiche e il resto per la difesa. Intanto tra i frugali, contrari a nuova flessibilità, il più esplicito è stato il ministro olandese Eelco Heinen, che si è detto "stanco" del tema: "Ogni volta che si presenta un problema sento sempre la stessa cosa: 'modifichiamo le regole fiscali'. Aggiungere debito al debito rende i problemi più grandi. Dobbiamo spendere meno e fare riforme. Fuggire dai problemi non è la soluzione".

items.title: Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis
items.summary: Hundreds have pitched their tents in central Madrid, while the Spanish prime minister has called a snap election.
items.content:
Pierina Nicuray, a 21-year-old university graduate, has spent a week camped out in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square.

Like many of the hundreds of others who have pitched their tents here to protest at Spain's housing crisis , she has no doubts when it comes to diagnosing the cause.

"It's the same problem as always," she says. "A lack of homes."

She adds: "Landlords are taking advantage of the situation to raise rentals, and then there's also Airbnb."

Jorge Moreno, a 19-year-old film-dubbing student who has also been living in a tent here in central Madrid for the last few days, agrees.

"There are so many homes standing empty because they have been bought by vulture funds and investment funds which hike up the rent of people living in properties until they get rid of them," says Jorge, who lives with his mother and fears it will be a long time before he can afford a home of his own.

"They've been making a business of housing for a long time," he adds. "But it's an abusive business which stops Spaniards from being able to live in a decent home."

His and Pierina's diagnoses are frequently voiced by fellow protesters, ordinary Spaniards and even the Spanish government.

On presenting a recent package of emergency measures to tackle the housing problem, Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he was legislating "against those who consider housing just another object on the market with which to speculate".

Those reforms were rejected by Congress, prompting Sánchez to call a snap election next month.

Nicuray and Moreno can point to the single case that sparked the current Spanish housing protest movement as proof that profit-driven practices are at the heart of the crisis: the 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home after the investment firm that had bought it tried to persuade her to leave, then sharply increased her rent, which she was unable to pay.

Although the social backlash that followed caused the company to invite Abascal to return to her old home, she never did, dying in hospital on Wednesday .

Many others have their own stories of struggling with a soaring rental market.

Carmen Pérez is a retired widow, originally from Ecuador, who has been living in Spain for 17 years.

When she arrived, housing was relatively cheap and accessible, but - as costs have risen - she has been forced to move in with her daughter and son-in-law as she looks for somewhere affordable to rent.

"When a property is listed to rent, there's always a long waiting list," she says. "And the rent is always too high for me. All of this has affected my health - I've got depression, I don't have any stability or security."

Spain has seen an average rise in rental costs of 84% over the last 10 years, according to property outlet Idealista.

In the centre of the southern city of Málaga, the increase has been 113 %, and, in Marbella - just under 150%.

A recent study by the Centre for Sociological Research (CIS) showed how the broader Spanish population, like the protesters, want to see action taken against those perceived to be powerful movers in the housing market.

Some 72% wanted higher taxes introduced for those with 10 or more properties; 76% wanted limits on short-term tourist accommodation; and 40% supported the expropriation of empty homes.

However, Jorge Galindo, director at the Esade centre for economic policy, says that available data makes it difficult to know exactly how many Spanish properties are owned by so-called "vulture funds" and being used for speculation.

He points to Bank of Spain figures from 2024 showing that only 8% of properties for rent are owned by companies.

Galindo says he concludes from the data available that there is not a notable accumulation of property to rent among a small number of owners in Spain.

"When it comes to explaining the rise in rentals, that is not the big cause," he says. "What explains it is the shortage of supply compared to demand over recent years."

The Bank of Spain appears to agree, and has estimated that the country has a housing shortfall of around 750,000 homes.

The institution's deputy governor, Soledad Núñez, warned in September that by 2028 that could rise to one million.

There are 3.8 million empty properties in Spain, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE), but a large number of those are in depopulated rural areas and therefore have little relevance to the current crisis, which is most acute in urban hubs.

Other explanations for this high number include properties awaiting renovation, or legal disputes between family members who have inherited them.

Demographic changes play a major part in the imbalance between supply and demand.

Between 2021 and 2025, there were about 1.2 million new households in Spain, driven in great part by the arrival of migrants who have played a major role in the country's recent economic growth.

However, house building has not kept pace, with fewer than half-a-million new homes during that period.

That was partly because Spain's construction industry had shrunk in the wake of the Eurozone crisis, while the cost of materials rose substantially after Covid, and a lack of political consensus put legal obstacles in the way of building.

"It was not a priority for us to build new houses," Galindo says. "But, once the demographic boom came, we realised how costly it was for us."

He adds that short-term tourist accommodation, like Airbnb, which has been identified by both the Spanish government and many activists as a culprit, is likely to have had a more localised effect, pushing up prices in specific urban areas rather than having an overall impact.

Meanwhile, the crisis has been aggravated by lagging salaries.

A study by El País found that, in real terms, the average Spaniard had 5% less spending power than a decade ago, due to taxes, social security and inflation. The average monthly salary in the Madrid region is €1,550 (£1,314; $1,738).

"No worker should have to spend 75% or 80% of their salary on rent, because what are they supposed to eat?" says Francisco Pardo, an 81-year-old retired taxi driver, who sympathises with the protesters, during a visit to the tent city in Madrid.

The case of Maricarmen has suddenly made the housing crisis an urgent topic of discussion, not just in Madrid's Puerta del Sol but across the country.

The question now is whether a consensus can be reached on how to solve it.

items.title: Il caso dei 30 secondi: 'La violenza sessuale prescinde dal tempo'
items.summary: I motivi della condanna in appello bis: 'Difesa passiva parte del trauma'. Vittima: 'Serve legge'
items.content:
Quei "20-30 secondi" non andavano nemmeno presi in considerazione , men che meno per sostenere, come fecero i giudici in due sentenze, che erano un tempo sufficiente per la vittima per reagire agli abusi. Erano, anzi, una finestra temporale indicata proprio dalla donna e con cui lei aveva " trasposto la sua percezione personale e dilatata del fatto ", tipica "reazione di chi sta subendo un fatto traumatico" . Voleva solo far capire quanto fosse stato rapido e improvviso ciò che aveva subito. E in tema di violenza sessuale non esiste "una soglia minima di durata" e si prescinde "dal tempo".

È con 31 pagine di motivazioni che la Corte d'Appello di Milano spiega perché il 10 luglio, nel processo di secondo grado bis, ha deciso di condannare a un anno e due mesi un ex sindacalista , che lavorava all'aeroporto di Malpensa, per violenza sessuale su una hostess che all'epoca, più di 8 anni fa, si era rivolta a lui per una vertenza sindacale . Il caso aveva suscitato polemiche perché con due sentenze, prima del Tribunale di Varese nel 2022 e poi dei giudici milanesi d'appello, il 48enne era stato assolto: la donna in quei "30 secondi", avevano scritto i magistrati, avrebbe potuto opporsi e "dileguarsi". Poi, la Cassazione nel febbraio 2025, dopo il ricorso del sostituto pg Angelo Renna, ha annullato con rinvio l'ultimo verdetto per il nuovo giudizio, in cui è stata accolta anche la linea della parte civile con l'avvocato Gionata Bonuccelli, che rappresenta la vittima.

"Ci sono voluti otto lunghi ed estenuanti anni per arrivare a questo risultato. Serve una legge che stabilisca nero su bianco che senza consenso è violenza. Sempre. Le donne italiane che denunciano non meritano il calvario che ho passato io", ha spiegato la 49enne ex hostess e ora insegnante. Sono nette le motivazioni dei giudici della seconda penale d'appello (collegio Manzi-Fasano-Galoppi). Da un lato, c'è "l'onere di accertarsi della sussistenza" del consenso e, dall'altro, "l'ordinamento non prevede una soglia minima di durata" della violenza che "prescinde dal tempo". Se si coglie "di sorpresa la vittima", l'azione rapida integra l'abuso impedendo di manifestare dissenso. E la "incredulità e il ritardo di pochi secondi nella reazione verbale non esprimono consenso", ma "difesa passiva" e "disorientamento, del tutto compatibile con il trauma subito".

Nel marzo 2018, la donna si era rivolta al sindacalista per una vertenza e durante quell'incontro, stando alle indagini, subì molestie e abusi. Nell'appello bis lei aveva testimoniato ancora una volta, confermando quanto messo a verbale dal primo giorno. Dichiarazioni sempre "attendibili". Il "ritardo nella reazione", ovvero "nella manifestazione del dissenso", aveva scritto la Cassazione motivando l'annullamento con rinvio, è "irrilevante" per la "configurazione della violenza". La Corte milanese ora ricorda proprio quei "principi di diritto irrinunciabili". E chiarisce che la Cassazione ha anche "inteso correttamente ricollegare al 'ritardo' nella reazione il fenomeno del 'freezing'", ossia il blocco fisico e emotivo per il trauma.

L'imputato, scrive la Corte, ha agito "vilmente avvicinandosi" in modo repentino e imprevedibile alle spalle "in un contesto lavorativo", mentre lei era "concentrata" su "ben altro". E se, poi, non ha "reagito 'immediatamente', cioè con la stessa prontezza con cui si ferma un oggetto che ci corre incontro" , ciò è del tutto privo di "significato". Anzi, lei una "reazione" l'ha avuta e ha mostrato "in modo arrabbiato, deciso e inequivocabile il proprio dissenso". Dissenso che, chiarisce la Corte, in "materia di libertà sessuale" deve essere sempre "presunto" e c'è, invece, l'onere di "accertarsi" del consenso "libero, attuale, specifico e perdurante". "Sembra semplice, oggi - ha spiegato il legale Bonuccelli -. Peccato siano stati necessari tre giudizi di merito ed uno di Cassazione, con oltre 6 anni e mezzo di battaglie giudiziarie , per accertarlo". In Cassazione, comunque, si andrà di nuovo, perché la difesa dovrebbe fare ricorso.

items.title: The value of not getting to the point (2015)
items.summary: Article URL: https://ken.arneson.name/2015/11/the-value-of-not-getting-to-the-point/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50010470 Points: 144 # Comments: 48
items.content:
I read somewhere recently, I forget where, that the purpose of people getting together for a conversation over a beer or coffee or lunch or dinner is that it the food and drink spare us from the burden of needing to have something to say throughout the whole conversation.

This was a revelation to me. All this time, I assumed that the primary purpose of lunch was lunch. All this time, I figured that I was just lousy at conversation because being an introvert made conversation awkward and laborious for me. For everyone else, conversation seems comparatively effortless. But it seems from this data that conversation must be harder for everyone else than I had assumed.

My oldest daughter is a freshman in college. She recently texted me and said she wanted to talk. I asked, what about? She got annoyed at me for asking.

I was clueless as to why. I guess the Dunning-Kruger effect applies to all of us, there’s always some area of life where we’re so incompetent we don’t even know we’re incompetent. This area, apparently, was one of mine.

She asked if we could just talk about something stupid. So I called her, and we talked about Donald Trump and the presidential race and stuff like that for a good long while. I didn’t ask about what was really bothering her.

Eventually, the conversation turned, and we finally got to talking about the thing she wanted to talk about. But that probably at least half an hour into the conversation. We segued slowly and organically from the stupid stuff into the real issue.

And this, too, was a bit of a revelation to me, that someone would not want to get straight to the point, that someone would need a nice long conversational warmup before they’d feel comfortable enough to be ready to talk about something more uncomfortable. I’m very much a get-to-the-point kind of person. I tend to say what I mean, or nothing at all.

Language is imprecise. Our feelings don’t always have direct translations into speech. It’s hard to explain what we feel, to say exactly what we mean. We have wants and desires and emotions, and we often try to rationalize those feelings. Those rationalizations are often logically incoherent. But it’s hard to see the incoherence of our own rationalizations because our points of view are so limited. And often (if we’re not falling prey to the Dunning-Kruger effect) we intuit that our rationalizations may be incoherent. So we’re cautious in what we say. We know that there can be social penalties for saying the wrong thing in the wrong way to the wrong person.

All this adds up to making the act of talking about something sensitive daunting. There is a vulnerability in speaking. That’s why our culture has all these rituals and conventions around conversation, like idle chit-chat and coffee and such: to build enough trust in the environment where we can feel comfortable enough to overcome the vulnerability inherent in speech.

I never fully understood this before. I feel like everyone else understands it, though, because they act as if they do. But if they do, it must be an intuitive understanding, a grokking, not an explicit fact that people state out loud. Otherwise, I probably would have heard someone say it explicitly sometime before in the almost 50 years I’ve been in this earth.

Having now finally come to this understanding, it occurs to me that perhaps this is the great flaw with Twitter, why everyone I know on Twitter seems to eventually run into a wall with it. The 140-character format pushes you to get straight to the point. There is no room for the idle chit-chat and sips of coffee and other conversational rituals that let us dance around the sensitive issues. Without these rituals that are built into real-life human-to-human conversation, the problems with speech that those cultural rituals are designed to prevent come flooding in.

There is so much hair pulling and teeth grinding about what people should and should not say online, and how they should or should not say it. And maybe all that hair pulling and teeth grinding arise because our online conversational cultures, and the technological platforms they reside on, have not had the time to evolve into something that works, the way that our real-life conversational culture has.

There are many, many more people who are clueless about how to behave in online conversations than there are people who are clueless about how to behave in offline ones. How I came to be the flipside of that, I don’t know.

And it also occurs to me that there is a value in stating explicitly the things that are mostly just intuited about human nature and human culture. I want to explore these sorts of things. There is a risk, though, a vulnerability, in stating these things. The people who intuitively grasp these things will feel as though I am insulting their intelligence by stating something so obvious it shouldn’t need saying. But it isn’t meant as an insult to their intelligence, it’s meant as an insult to mine. I need to say these things because I’m the one who doesn’t understand these things. I need them explained to myself.

Which is all a roundabout way of stating something that maybe could fit into a tweet: I plan to start saying things that aren’t obvious to me but may be obvious to others. Sorry if you fall into the latter category and I waste your time. Such is the risk of saying anything, ever. And sorry for the roundaboutness in getting to this point. I seemed to need it, for some strange reason.
